hints: This answer names a sacred object rather than a person or place.

hints: This answer describes a dramatic sign, not a permanent location.

hints: This answer names a body of water tied to Israel's escape story.

A path appeared here where there should not have been one.
Pharaoh's army was overwhelmed when the waters returned.
rounds.teachingNote: The Red Sea fits because Exodus 14 says the waters divided for Israel and returned over Pharaoh's army.

hints: This answer names a river rather than a city or mountain.

hints: This answer is an indoor place connected with a small gathered group.

Followers of Jesus were told to gather and remain together here.

rounds.teachingNote: The upper room connects the Last Supper setting in Luke 22 with the gathered believers waiting in prayer in Acts 1.

hints: This answer is a parable figure, not a historical officeholder.

His actions mattered more than the religious status of those who passed by.
Religious passersby failed where this traveler acted.
Jesus used this character to redefine neighbor love.
rounds.teachingNote: Luke 10 identifies the Good Samaritan as the unexpected neighbor who stopped, showed mercy, and cared for the wounded man.

hints: This answer names a preacher whose ministry prepared for someone greater.

rounds.teachingNote: John the Baptist fits the clues because Matthew 3 presents him preaching repentance, baptizing in the Jordan, and preparing the way for Jesus.

hints: This answer is a woman whose position gave her access in a dangerous court.

A threat against her people forced her to act.
Her courage involved timing, banquets, and an unsummoned approach.
She helped stop Haman's plot against the Jews.
rounds.teachingNote: Esther's danger and courage are anchored in Esther 4 and 7, where she risks approaching the king and exposes Haman's plot.

rounds.teachingNote: David is the shepherd chosen and anointed in 1 Samuel 16, then recognized as king over Israel in 2 Samuel 5.

hints: This answer names a major New Testament missionary.
His ministry followed a complete redirection of life.

He carried the gospel across cities in the Roman world.
His ministry followed a dramatic conversion and years of travel.

rounds.teachingNote: Paul's clues point to his Damascus-road conversion in Acts 9 and his missionary calling from Antioch in Acts 13.

hints: This answer is a group of commands rather than a person or place.

hints: This answer is a meal remembered for both fellowship and coming sorrow.
It took place during the final approach to the crucifixion.
This meal is remembered for bread, cup, and betrayal in the same room.

It took place shortly before Jesus was arrested.
It is the final Passover meal Jesus shared with his disciples.
rounds.teachingNote: The Last Supper is the Passover meal where Jesus shared bread and cup with His disciples before His arrest.

hints: This answer is an object connected to a national failure in worship.
It became a symbol of impatience while Moses was absent.
This object exposed impatience while Moses was away.
The people turned visible wealth into a false center of devotion.
Aaron's involvement made the failure especially costly.
Israel worshiped this image at Sinai.
rounds.teachingNote: Exodus 32 identifies the golden calf as Israel's idol made while Moses was on Sinai, explaining the clues about Aaron, worship, and judgment.

hints: This answer is a building project remembered for judgment, not completion.

Human pride and collective ambition drive this story.
Its builders wanted unity and fame on their own terms.
Its builders wanted a name for themselves and a city that would hold them together.
God answered by confusing language and scattering the people.
rounds.teachingNote: Genesis 11 says Babel was built to make a name for the people before God confused their language and scattered them.

hints: This answer is a future image rather than an ancient battlefield or object.

It is presented as a city prepared by God, not built by human effort.

An older brother and a patient father sharpen the lesson.

Jesus used this son to picture repentance and grace.
rounds.teachingNote: The prodigal son is the younger son in Luke 15 who squandered his inheritance and was welcomed home by his father.

hints: This answer is a small image used to explain a large outcome.

Its size is part of the lesson, not just its species.

hints: This answer is a mission statement rather than a miracle or title.

rounds.teachingNote: Matthew 28 anchors the Great Commission, where Jesus sends His disciples to make disciples, baptize, and teach all nations.

hints: This answer is a metaphor Jesus used in conversation, not a literal supply.

A discussion at a well made the image unforgettable.
A conversation at a well made it especially memorable.
Jesus used it to speak about life that satisfies forever.
rounds.teachingNote: Jesus speaks of living water in John 4 and John 7, tying the image to eternal life and the Spirit.

hints: This answer is a title Jesus used for himself.

It appears in a discourse after a miracle meal.
Jesus used this phrase in John 6.
rounds.teachingNote: John 6:35 identifies Jesus as the bread of life, the source of lasting satisfaction for those who come to Him.

sessions.title: Prophets And Practice
sessions.theme: Images of endurance, worship, and discipleship

hints: This answer names character produced by God's Spirit.

hints: This answer is a prophetic scene rather than a simple teaching phrase.

hints: This answer is a mountain linked to a showdown over worship.

hints: This answer describes a small gift that carried great spiritual weight.

Jesus used it to expose the difference between appearance and devotion.
